terra.problem: The verse describes seeking God with the whole heart; it does not contrast that with offerings at an altar.
The tidy-kitchen joke has no clear connection to the verse's description of walking in God's ways and doing no iniquity.
“He's not hiding anything” asserts more about the writer than the passage says.
Calling winning every argument a handy side effect suggests that hiding God's word in the heart would produce that result. The text does not say so.
The explanation is flat and generic, repeating the answer without a distinctive Papa Dorin line.
The explanation repeats the verse's purpose without adding much insight or Papa Dorin's personality.
It says the writer sees wonders in God's law. The verse records his request to see them, not that he has seen them.
Calling God's law a nicer view than the faces of the writer's enemies risks putting down people's appearance.
Verse 17 mentions one servant, the writer, not servants.
The verse says the writer meditates on God's statutes, but it does not say he isn't trading insults.
The claim that enemies appear elsewhere in the psalm needs a reference, such as Psalm 119:98.
The verse does not say the writer is talking about the testimonies out loud.
